source: lab (real recording, background replaced by a synthetic snowy-sky image via Segment Anything 2; 'Modified with Segment Anything 2 Demo' watermark bottom-right)

camera.motion: static (background pixels change < 0.1% between any two consecutive frames; table outline fixed)
camera.view: slightly above table-top height, looking roughly horizontally at a table; the table top is seen as a trapezoid (back edge short and high in the image, front edge long and low), so image-down = toward the camera on the table plane
camera.perspective_cues: table-top trapezoid: back edge y~441-450 from x~403 to ~765 (length ~362 px), front edge y~590-598 from x~188 to ~997 (length ~809 px); the side edges converge upward to a vanishing point above the table (left edge back-left(403,442)->front-left(188,590), right edge back-right(765,450)->front-right(997,598)). Horizon is about at/above the back edge (camera only slightly higher than the table top).

objects.name: ball
objects.description: the only moving object: small white/cream ball (looks like a ping-pong-size ball), white highlight on top, grey shading underneath, thin bright segmentation halo around it
objects.visible_frames: 0-39 fully/mostly (39 bottom cut by watermark box), 40 only a 3-px sliver above the watermark, 41-48 gone
objects.reference_point: centroid of the ball mask (cx, cy) = visible centre

apparent_size_px.note: use width_across_main_axis or bbox_h (motion is mostly horizontal on the table) as the diameter proxy; the length along the motion direction includes motion blur
